p:cNvPr.descr: A structural comparison of 2 membrane lipid structures. Both membrane lipids have a long double carbon chain on the left, bonded right to a phosphocholine. The top molecule, phosphatidylcholine, has 2 long parallel, horizontal carbon chains. The top chain has 21 carbons and the bottom chain has 18. The bottom carbon chain has 2 bottom cis double bonds at the 9th-10th and 12th-13th carbons in the chain. On the far right, the first C in the chain double bonds down to O, up and right to O, which dashed wedge bonds up to C. C solid wedge bonds down to H, up and right to C, which bonds down and right to O. O bonds right to the phosphocholine, whose structure will be explained. The top carbon chain double bonds up to O on its 4th carbon from the right, bonds down and right to O, which is part of the chain, and O bonds up and right to C, which bonds down to C. This C dashed wedge bonds down to O and solid wedge bonds down to H before bonding up and right to C. C bonds down and right to O, which bonds up and right to the P in phosphocholine. The phosphocholine is shaded blue. It consists of a central P bonded down and left to O, double bonded up to O, down to O-, and down and right to O. The O bonds down and right to C, which bonds up and right to C, which bonds down and right to N+, which has 3 bonds to the upper right, right, and lower right. The second molecule, sphingomyelin, is shown below. It consists of 2 long parallel, horizontal carbon chains on the left. The top chain has 18 carbons and the bottom chain has 16. There is a double bond between the 4th and 5th carbons on the top chain leads right to C, which bonds up and right to C, which dashed wedge bonds up to H and solid wedge bonds up to OH. The C bonds down and right to C, which dashed wedge bonds down to NH and solid wedge bonds down to H. The C bonds up and right to C, then bonds down and right to O. This marks the begining of the phosphocholine. The NH on the top chain bonds down and left to C, which double bonds down to O, and bonds left to the remainder of the chain, which has no double bonds or susbtituents.
